title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. pi = pi_{0,3} = pi_1(U_{0,3}) is free of rank 2, with U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,infinity}. The groups E = S_{0,3} = pi_1(U_{0,3}, T_{0,3}) are extensions of the automorphism group G = T_{0,3} ≅ S_3 x Z/2 by pi; the Z/2 factor is complex conjugation. These are the 'cartographic' groups. The non-oriented triangular cartographic group is C_2*C_2*C_2 = <tau_0, tau_1, tau_inf | tau_i^2 = 1>. Its even-length index-2 subgroup is pi, generated by l_0 = tau_inf tau_1, l_1 = tau_0 tau_inf, l_inf = tau_1 tau_0, with l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1.

What the 'equations des lacets' are. Grothendieck studies the equations g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1 for rho of order 3 (cyclic rotation of 0, 1, inf) and h sigma(h) = 1 for sigma_inf of order 2 (z -> 1-z). These are exactly the later 3-cycle and 2-cycle relations of the Drinfeld/Ihara Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^. He treats them as non-abelian 1-cocycle conditions for Z/n acting on pi.

The general principle (from the previous pages). Solutions g correspond to lifts g·rho of order n in pi ⋊ <rho>. Pi-conjugacy classes of such lifts, i.e. the non-abelian H^1(Z/n, pi), correspond to fixed points of the automorphism on U_{0,3}. The stabiliser of a class is pi^rho, which is trivial.

The order-3 case (rho). The fixed points are -j and -jbar, so there are two classes. Each class is a pi-torsor, since pi^rho = 1. Complex conjugation tau_inf swaps the two classes. Hence the full solution set of (32) is in bijection with E' = pi·{1, tau_inf}, the non-oriented triangulated cartographic group, via beta -> beta rho(beta)^{-1}. Formula (34) computes the base solution of the second class: tau_inf rho(tau_inf)^{-1} = l_1^{-1}. This follows from rho_inf = tau_inf rho tau_inf^{-1} = l_1^{-1} rho = rho l_0^{-1}. It is a valid solution, since l_1^{-1} l_inf^{-1} l_0^{-1} = (l_0 l_inf l_1)^{-1} = 1.

The profinite extension. He conjectures the same holds after profinite completion, provided two things hold:
- (33) the rho-fixed subgroup of hat{pi~}_{0,3} is trivial;
- every finite-order element of hat S_{0,3} is conjugate to a finite-order element of the discrete S_{0,3}.

The order-2 case (sigma_inf). The fixed locus of z -> 1-z on U_{0,3} is the single point 1/2. Hence every solution of h sigma(h) = 1 is uniquely a coboundary h = beta sigma(beta)^{-1} with beta in pi; that is, non-abelian H^1(Z/2, pi) is trivial and pi^sigma = 1. The next page notes that if beta is allowed to range over S_{0,3}, the ambiguity is the Klein four-group generated by sigma_inf and tau_inf.

Purpose. This parametrises solutions of the GT-type relations, i.e. the components of elements of the Teichmüller-tower automorphism group, as coboundaries. It is the first step toward describing Gal(Qbar/Q), or its combinatorial envelope, via pairs (lambda, f) in F^_2.
errors: No mathematical error found. The claim pi^{sigma_inf} = 1 is correct. The quotient orbifold P^1 - {0,1,inf} modulo z -> 1-z has orbifold pi_1 ≅ Z * Z/2, and a finite free factor is self-centralising, so the centraliser of sigma in pi is trivial.
(34) is consistent with (23), assuming rho(x) = rho x rho^{-1} and tau_inf^2 = 1.
Gap, acknowledged by Grothendieck himself: the profinite statements (33) and the conjugacy of finite-order elements are explicitly left 'à vérifier ultérieurement'.

ideas.what: The 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 and g rho(g) rho^2(g)=1 in pi_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}) read as non-abelian 1-cocycle conditions for Z/2 and Z/3.
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological interpretation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Lochak and L. Schneps, 'A cohomological interpretation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group' (Invent. Math. 1997), building on Drinfeld 1990 and Ihara
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche as far as known; unsure whether this specific cocycle viewpoint was circulated.

ideas.what: Classes of solutions (non-abelian H^1(Z/n, pi)) correspond to fixed points of the finite automorphism on U_{0,3}: two classes (-j, -jbar) for rho, one class (1/2) for sigma_inf.
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian H^1 of a finite group acting on an orbifold pi_1 ↔ conjugacy classes of torsion lifts ↔ fixed points (discrete analogue of section/Sullivan-type correspondences)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in orbifold / free-product theory (Kurosh subgroup theorem); in the GT context, Lochak–Schneps

ideas.what: Uniform parametrisation of all solutions of the 3-cycle equation by the non-oriented cartographic group pi·{1, tau_inf}, i.e. g = beta rho(beta)^{-1} with beta in E', with base solution l_1^{-1} for the second class.
Assumption that torsion elements of the profinite completion of the cartographic group are conjugate to discrete ones, and that fixed subgroups stay trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Conjugacy of torsion in free profinite products / profinite completions of virtually free groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herfort–Ribes (1985, torsion and centralisers in free profinite products); C. Scheiderer, appendix to Lochak–Schneps 1997

missed.claim: Grothendieck, around 1981 and before Drinfeld's GT (1990), formulates the 2-cycle and 3-cycle 'loop equations' as non-abelian cocycle equations. He solves the 2-cycle one in the discrete case as unique coboundaries h = beta sigma(beta)^{-1}, using the unique fixed point 1/2. He parametrises all solutions of the 3-cycle one by the non-oriented cartographic group, using the two fixed points -j and -jbar and complex conjugation. This is essentially the content later published by Lochak–Schneps (1997) as the cohomological interpretation of GT^.
missed.quote: toute solution de l'équation correspondante (35) h σ_∞(h)=1 se met sous la forme standard (36) h=β σ_∞(β)^{-1} et ceci de façon unique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an earlier, geometric origin (via fixed points of automorphisms of U_{0,3} and cartographic groups) of a result credited to Lochak–Schneps. It is a priority/attribution point and suggests a fixed-point method for higher U_{0,n}.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly isolates the needed profinite inputs: triviality of rho-fixed subgroups in the completion, and that torsion of the completion is conjugate to discrete torsion. He leaves them to be checked. These were later established, e.g. Herfort–Ribes and Scheiderer's appendix, apparently independently of these notes.
missed.quote: si on admet (chose à vérifier ultérieurement) (33) ... et que les éléments d'ordre fini de Ŝ_{0,3} sont conjugués des éléments d'ordre fini de S_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The programme of extending the fixed-point/cocycle picture to the full Teichmüller tower, i.e. finite automorphisms of U_{0,n} and U_{g,n} with profinite torsion-conjugacy, is in the spirit of later work on GT^ and torsion in profinite mapping class groups, but was not developed systematically from this viewpoint.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a notable unpublished anticipation of the Lochak–Schneps cohomological interpretation of the GT^ relations, including the exact profinite torsion-conjugacy hypothesis that Scheiderer later proved. It also includes the geometric fixed-point explanation. The result itself is now known, so this is a priority/connection point rather than new mathematics.
